question: A 57-year-old woman with a history of diabetes and hypertension accidentally overdoses on antiarrhythmic medication. Upon arrival in the ER, she is administered a drug to counteract the effects of the overdose. Which of the following matches an antiarrhythmic with its correct treatment in overdose?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Quinidine overdose" -> "hypoglycemia" -> "insulin counteracts hypoglycemia" -> "stabilizes blood sugar levels" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Encainide overdose" -> "cardiac arrhythmias" -> "epinephrine stabilizes heart rate" -> "restores normal cardiac function" -> 65%
CHAIN: "Propafenone overdose" -> "hypoglycemia" -> "glucose elevates blood sugar" -> "counteracts hypoglycemic effects" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Esmolol overdose" -> "bradycardia" -> "glucagon increases heart rate" -> "counteracts bradycardia" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Sotalol overdose" -> "hypotension and bradycardia" -> "norepinephrine increases blood pressure and heart rate" -> "restores cardiovascular stability" -> 85%
analysis: In cases of beta-blocker overdose, such as with esmolol, glucagon is often used as an antidote. Glucagon can help reverse the negative effects on heart rate and blood pressure by increasing intracellular cyclic AMP and improving cardiac contractility and conduction. The other options do not correctly match the antiarrhythmic drugs with their respective treatments for overdose.
